new_statements.quote: p. 418: "Stress in Bul falls on the penult unless there is a paragogic vowel, in which case it falls on the antepenult. Loss of the paragogic syllable in Bul therefore results in regular penult stress." — note 15, p. 425: "The Holle list (Stokhof 1983:139-181) shows stress placement in Bul. This is identical with the word stress pattern in Kdp. It is probable that in pre-PGtl stress regularly fell on the penult. With the development of the paragogic vowel stress thus became unpredictable (as in Kdp and, until this change, in Bul). In Gtl stress again became regular by shifting from the antepenult to the penult in words containing a paragogic syllable."

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog's penult rule (penultimate stress) and as Machmoed 1973 (already held by the project, thesis pp. 19-20: stress 'always falls on the penult'). Adds the historical framing (regularisation from antepenult to penult in paragogic-vowel words) and the contrast with Buol/Kaidipang. The Gorontalo data are from the dialect of Gorontalo city (p. 408). Live Brill URL returns an AWS WAF 'Human Verification' page (not reachable by automated download); the PDF was downloaded from the the Internet Archive capture of 2020-02-09 of that same URL (21 pp, KITLV-journals scan with text layer; stress passages verified against the page images).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Gorontalo (Gtl) word stress is regular on the penultimate syllable, including in words that end in the historical paragogic vowel -o (where the sister languages Buol and Kaidipang keep antepenult stress). The authors reconstruct regular penult stress for pre-Proto-Gorontalic, an intermediate stage with unpredictable (antepenult-before-paragogic-vowel) stress, and a Gorontalo shift back to the penult.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Gorontalo. The antepenult-before-paragogic-vowel pattern is stated for Buol (p. 418) and Kaidipang (note 15), not for Gorontalo. Note 16 adds that loss of *ʔ between identical vowels gave long vowels whose phonemic status 'has not yet been examined'.
new_statements.identity_note: Sneddon and Usup 1986 use data 'from the dialect of Gorontalo city' (p. 408). The Zorc bundle's worksheet names informants Hamzah Machmoed and Asma Mustafa (Gorontalo, elicited by A. John Little Jr.); the handwritten notes themselves name no dialect. Statements about Buol (Bul) and Kaidipang (Kdp) in Sneddon and Usup concern other Gorontalic languages.

audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-dominant penultimate, penultimate stress) rests on a Wikipedia sentence paraphrasing Little 1995:523; we held no file. I downloaded the Wikipedia wikitext and confirmed the sentence and its Little 1995 p.523 footnote verbatim, and downloaded Joest 1883 (archive.org), whose sec. 4 independently states penultimate accent that moves rightward with suffixes (wadala / wadala-mu / wadala-lio) with a footnote listing a few final-stress exceptions (-ao > -a contractions, kiki-no) - consistent with non-strict 'fixed-dominant' penult. Nothing seen contradicts the classification, so not at-risk; but the evidence chain is second-hand and sketch-level while a dedicated phonology article (Steinhauer 1991, paywalled Brill, verified Restricted Access), a 386-pp dissertation grammar (Little 1978) and a 74-pp phonology thesis (Machmoed 1973) exist unconsulted. Action: obtain Steinhauer 1991 and/or L
